symptom: `find $l by Other.Person_Dept = $d` over HR.Emp (HR.Emp extends Other.Person) built clean, but describe printed `find $l by Person_Dept = $d`; executed as a new microflow that passed check -p and exec and mxbuild then failed `[CE1613] "The selected attribute 'HR.Emp.Person_Dept' no longer exists."` (11.12.5). A hand-written bare inherited association in a find or a create's members stored the same attribute (ako/mxcli#1637)
cause: An association lives in its FROM entity's module, so one inherited from a generalization in another module is not in the specialization's module. resolveMemberChange looked a bare name up only there, then fell through to an attribute of the entity. resolveAttributeInEntityHierarchy already walked the chain for attributes; nothing did for associations
file: `mdl/executor/cmd_microflows_builder_actions.go` (`resolveInheritedAssociation`, tried after the inherited-attribute lookup in resolveMemberChange's bare-name branch)
insight: Fix the reader the short form is executed by, not the printer: describe has no variable types for a list operation, but the builder knows the entity, so making the bare name resolve through the chain makes describe's existing output correct, leaves every describe golden untouched, and lets the member speller (which shortens only when the short name resolves to the same member) agree with describe for free — its test was the cheapest proof, the round trip needs a FRESH build because re-running over the stored flow is spliced as 'Unchanged'. Assert on the stored unit bytes (`HR.Emp.Person_Dept` absent, `Other.Person_Dept` present): describe prints attribute and association alike, so it cannot show the damage. Not covered: the same bare name in two modules on one chain still resolves to the entity's own module first, and check -p still passes a member that names nothing
